# Count the Dots

> A free tally counter for anything you can be bothered to count. Three buttons —
> blue, yellow and red — stamp the current time when tapped, and a chart shows how
> many of each you got per hour, day, week or over the whole log.

Count the Dots is a web app that installs to a phone's home screen as a PWA and
works with no network connection. It has no accounts, no server and no sync: every
click is stored in the browser's own `localStorage` on the device that recorded it,
and nothing is ever transmitted anywhere.

## What it is for

People use it as a tally counter, habit tracker, symptom log or field-notes
counter — counting coffees, cigarettes, reps, pain levels from 1 to 3, birds,
passing cars, or interruptions during a working day. The app never asks what the
colours mean.

## How it works

- Tap blue, yellow or red. Each tap records a timestamp.
- The timeline plots how many clicks each colour got per period — plain integer
  counts, not a running total and not a smoothed rate.
- An event rail under the chart marks every individual tap at its exact time.
- Ranges: today, 7 days, 30 days, or all time.
- Export and import as JSON; import replaces whole days rather than merging.

## Privacy

There is no server component. No account is required, no analytics run inside the
app, and no click data leaves the device. Clearing the browser's site data deletes
the log, which is why the app ships an export button.
